newsitem.title: USA: Judge allows Louisiana trial to proceed against Dow.
newsitem.headline: Judge allows Louisiana trial to proceed against Dow.

text.p: A federal judge ruled on Wednesday that the first two phases of a Louisiana class action breast implant suit by 1,700 women against Dow Chemical Inc. can proceed.

U.S. District Court Judge Denise Page Hood granted part of an emergency plaintiff request that she abstain from the two-month-old trial, which had been halted by an appeals court ruling earlier this month.

In her opinion, Hood accepted arguments from plaintiff attorneys that not granting their motion for a "mandatory abstention" would result in an untimely delay of the trial. The trial, which began jury selection on March 17, has generated 5,000 pages of testimony and arguments and about 300 exhibits.
"The judicial system's high regard for the jury's service must be kept intact. Discharging the jury at this time would defeat this aim," Judge Hood wrote.

The case is one of the first class action suits to go to trial against the Midland, Mich.-based chemical giant. The trial was halted when the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals ruled May 8 that all state and federal implant suits against Dow Chemical, Dow Corning Corp. and Corning Inc. should be consolidated in federal court in Detroit.

Dow Chemical and Corning each own 50 percent of Dow Corning, which is operating under bankruptcy court protection. Thousands of women have alleged the implants cause numerous health problems, including lupus and rheumatoid arthritis.
